key_insight: HalluGuard disentangles and quantifies two distinct hallucination sources—data-driven and reasoning-driven—providing a unified, task-agnostic risk score and attribution that improves detection and mitigation of LLM hallucinations.
problem_solved: Current hallucination detection approaches handle either data or reasoning errors and rely on task-specific heuristics; this paper addresses the need for a general, source-aware detection and attribution method that generalizes across tasks and domains.
method: Design diagnostic probes and interventions that separate data-driven failures (false or missing knowledge) from reasoning-driven failures (logical or chain-of-thought mistakes).
Compute a unified hallucination risk score with per-source attribution so practitioners can detect, prioritize, and explain failures.
Provide a model-agnostic evaluation pipeline (e.g., contrastive inputs, chain-of-thought checks, and counterfactual tests) to validate detection across tasks and domains.
impact: Enables developers and researchers to detect, attribute, and prioritize hallucination remediation more effectively across domains (healthcare, law, science), improving LLM reliability and trustworthiness in high-stakes settings.
visual_elements: Two-branch flowchart: left branch labeled Data-Driven (missing/incorrect facts), right branch labeled Reasoning-Driven (logic/chain-of-thought errors); arrows converge to a unified risk score.
Stacked bar chart or heatmap comparing traditional single-source detectors vs HalluGuard's attribution-aware risk scores across several tasks.
Example prompt → model output → annotated failure map showing which tokens/errors are attributed to data vs reasoning.
Icon set: shield (safety), magnifying glass (diagnostics), scales (attribution), and an adjustable meter (risk score)
paper_title: HalluGuard: Demystifying Data-Driven and Reasoning-Driven Hallucinations in LLMs
paper_authors: Xinyue Zeng, Junhong Lin, Yujun Yan, Feng Guo, Liang Shi
